mcqs.q: Validation showed litter clump weight could be used as a marker of what?
mcqs.e: Clump weight was significantly predicted by the volume of water added, validating it as a proxy for crude urine output.

mcqs.q: How did urine clump weight change after Day 1 in newly admitted cats, and what did this imply?
o: Increased significantly, implying initial Day 1 suppression from acute stress
mcqs.e: Clump weight rose significantly after Day 1, indicating urine was acutely suppressed on Day 1, likely from the stress of moving.

mcqs.q: How well did the support vector machine classify cats at risk of urine suppression?
mcqs.e: The SVM had modest training accuracy (~81.8-86.3%) across suppression cutoffs, suggesting limited but real predictive ability.

mcqs.q: When were stress-related behaviors lowest in cats placed in an unfamiliar environment?
o: When alone with a scent object
mcqs.e: Cats showed fewer stress behaviors with the owner present, supporting a Secure Base Effect.

mcqs.q: Did an owner-scented object reduce cat anxiety the way owner presence did?
o: No, the scent object did not reduce stress
mcqs.e: The calming effect was seen only with the owner present, not when the cat was alone with the scent object.

mcqs.q: Cat Stress Scores were significantly higher in which group?
mcqs.e: CSS was significantly higher in single- versus multi-cat households, suggesting more acute stress signs in single-cat cats.

mcqs.q: Did reported agonistic interactions within multi-cat households affect CSS?
mcqs.e: CSS did not vary with reports of agonistic interactions among cohabiting cats.

mcqs.q: How many factors did principal component analysis reduce the cat-owner relationship items to?
mcqs.e: PCA reduced items to four factors, including owner emotional investment and cat aloofness/proximity needs.

mcqs.q: The study concluded the type of cat-owner bond is primarily the product of what?
o: The dynamic between both individuals plus personality and owner expectations
Whether the cat is indoor or outdoor
mcqs.e: The bond emerges from the dynamic between cat and owner, shaped by sociability and owner expectations.

mcqs.q: How many behavior/personality factors did the questionnaire identify?
mcqs.e: Factor analysis yielded seven traits, e.g., fearfulness, activity/playfulness, aggression and sociability toward humans.

mcqs.q: What did the validation analyses conclude about owner-completed questionnaires?
o: They were unreliable and should be abandoned
Validity and reliability were good, strengthening them as a data method
mcqs.e: Internal consistency, test-retest and inter-rater reliability were good, supporting owner questionnaires as valid tools.

mcqs.q: Breed differences in the traits were interpreted as suggesting what?
mcqs.e: Breed-paralleled trait differences suggest a genetic basis for feline personality.

mcqs.q: Did most cats appear ill before eating plants?
o: No, very few showed signs of illness
mcqs.e: Very few cats showed signs of illness before plant eating, arguing against the 'feeling ill' hypothesis.

mcqs.q: What finding argued against the hairball-expelling hypothesis?
o: Short-haired cats ate plants as often as long-haired cats
mcqs.e: Since short-haired cats ate plants as frequently as long-haired cats, plant eating is unlikely to be for expelling hair.

mcqs.q: Compared with older cats, young cats showed what pattern of plant eating?
o: Ate plants less and vomited more
Ate plants more frequently and appeared ill/vomited less
mcqs.e: Young cats consumed plants more often yet appeared ill and vomited less, suggesting it is normal behavior, not illness-driven.

mcqs.q: Frequency of laser light play was significantly associated with what?
o: Most surveyed abnormal repetitive behaviors (except overgrooming)
mcqs.e: Laser play frequency correlated with all surveyed ARBs apart from overgrooming.

mcqs.q: Which cats were more likely to display abnormal repetitive behaviors?
mcqs.e: Indoor-only access and young age (1-2 years) were significant predictors of reported ARBs.

mcqs.q: Which body feature best predicted the outcome of cat-cat interactions?
mcqs.e: Ear position was critical: both cats with erect ears predicted a positive outcome, while other positions predicted negative outcomes.

mcqs.q: The 'tail-up' display was most notably used by cats in which context?
o: When approaching a human, often preceding rubbing
mcqs.e: Tail-up was important when a cat approached a human and typically led to rubbing on the person's legs.

mcqs.q: A model in this review predicted that degree of kitten socialization has major consequences for what?
mcqs.e: Socialization status as a kitten shapes later responses to unfamiliar humans, with enormous consequences for shelter adoptions.

mcqs.q: What did the author argue is needed before prescribing certain breeds for animal-assisted interventions?
o: Reliable direct observational data on breed differences
Genetic testing of all therapy cats
mcqs.e: Breed differences from subjective ratings must be corroborated by direct observation before relying on them for interventions.

mcqs.q: Urinary cortisol and oxytocin levels were significantly higher under which condition?
mcqs.e: Both metabolites were higher in the non-social condition, where cats had no social contact with humans.

mcqs.q: What did the authors infer from the hormonal results?
o: Cats recognize social interaction with humans as important
Oxytocin cannot be measured in cat urine
mcqs.e: Higher stress-related hormones without human contact suggest cats value social interaction with humans.

mcqs.q: Did using a ball-type food toy versus a food bowl affect owner-perceived quality of life during weight loss?
o: Yes, the food toy improved QOL
Yes, the food toy worsened QOL
mcqs.e: No effect of food toy versus bowl on owner-perceived QOL was detected.

mcqs.q: How did owner-perceived QOL at the final weigh-in compare with the initial?
mcqs.e: Owner-perceived QOL was higher at the end of the weight loss plan than at the start.

mcqs.q: What was usually needed for cats to eat the low-calorie vegetables offered for satiety?
mcqs.e: 28 of 32 cats ate vegetables only with a palatability additive; just 4 ate them plain.

mcqs.q: Qualitative Behaviour Assessment PC1 ranged along what dimension?
mcqs.e: PC1 reflected emotional valence, from calm/relaxed/friendly to tense/fearful/alert.

mcqs.q: How did QBA outcomes relate to the quantitative coding-method temperament results?
o: QBA PC1 was significantly correlated with the coding-method results
QBA failed to identify any components
mcqs.e: QBA PC1 correlated significantly with the main coding-method temperament outcomes, supporting QBA as a valid tool.
